docs.title: Approve releases before production jobs
docs.text:
A freshly deployed hub runs no production jobs until an evaluation of each (execution profile, platform) has been promoted on this hub (Releases); jobs submitted before that wait with queue_reason: release_not_approved. With the Mac worker online, run per profile the clients use (private-auto is the organization default, mac-private the worker profile):

export RESONA_API_URL=https://resona.ecsplico.de RESONA_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.resona/hub-admin.token)
resona eval --profile private-auto --remote --output-dir /tmp/eval-private-auto
resona eval promote <evaluation-id> --report /tmp/eval-private-auto/report.json   # pins eval/baselines.json; commit it

Queued jobs are claimed as soon as the promotion lands. resona-admin worker approve on the hub, /ready, and GET /v1/baselines?execution_profile=private-auto&platform=mac-metal show the state (404 baseline_required until promoted).

docs.title: Provision credentials
docs.text:
resona-admin runs inside the hub container: ssh <user>@<coolify-host> docker exec -i <app-uuid>-hub-1 resona-admin .... Without SSH, use a Coolify scheduled task on the hub container (<app-uuid>-hub-1), execute it once, then delete it. The container's root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is a tmpfs. Generate tokens on your own machine and register only their SHA-256 hash, so the tokens never reach the server or its logs:

# on your machine
(umask 077; python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))' > ~/.resona/hub-client.token)
shasum -a 256 < <(tr -d '\n' < ~/.resona/hub-client.token) | cut -d' ' -f1

# in the hub container
resona-admin organization create ecsplico
resona-admin credential issue --organization ecsplico --role client --token-sha256 <hex>
resona-admin worker enroll mac-studio --organization ecsplico --token-sha256 <hex>
resona-admin worker approve <worker-id> --private --capabilities-file caps.json

A=<app-uuid>
coolify app task create $A --name admin --container $A-hub-1 --frequency "0 0 1 1 *" \
  --command "resona-admin organization create ecsplico"
coolify app task execute $A <task-uuid>
coolify app task executions $A <task-uuid> --format json   # "status": "success"
coolify app task update $A <task-uuid> --command "<next resona-admin command>"   # repeat
coolify app task delete $A <task-uuid>

The task command is limited to about 250 characters. worker approve needs the capabilities file inside the container: write it to /tmp within the same command, for example python -c "import base64,zlib;open('/tmp/c.json','wb').write(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode('<b64>')))" && resona-admin worker approve ..., split over several executions if needed. Check the result from your machine: GET /v1/settings with the new client token returns 200, and a worker heartbeat returns its approved_capabilities.

Without --token-sha256, resona-admin generates the token and prints it once into the task output, so prefer the hash.

docs.title: Restore a backup
docs.text:
Back up the database with the SQLite backup API while the hub runs (never by copying the file), for example from the hub container:

python -c "import sqlite3; s=sqlite3.connect('/data/db/jjobs.sqlite'); d=sqlite3.connect('/data/backup.sqlite'); s.backup(d)"

Payload directories are transient and are not backed up.

Restore only while the hub is stopped. resona-admin restore refuses to run while a hub holds the lock file next to the database:

coolify app stop <app-uuid>
# on the server: one-off container on the same volume
docker run --rm -v <resona-data volume>:/data <hub image> resona-admin restore /data/backup.sqlite
coolify app start <app-uuid>

The restore:

  1. copies the backup over the database with the SQLite backup API and migrates it to the current schema;
  2. revokes every restored credential and worker. A credential that was revoked after the backup was taken therefore cannot come back. Issue fresh credentials and re-enroll the workers afterwards;
  3. invalidates every active lease: processing jobs are requeued, or failed when no attempt or time is left;
  4. marks jobs whose payload files are gone as content_unavailable: pending jobs without input fail with that code, and completed jobs without a result file answer 410 content_unavailable on the result route. Results are never fabricated;
  5. runs one maintenance pass, which reapplies content and metadata retention before the hub serves requests.

It prints counts only, never identifiers of content.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: The hub and MCP containers log request lines without query strings, plus counts from the maintenance loop. They never log transcripts, Markdown, original filenames or tokens. Reading the container logs through the Coolify API or CLI (coolify app logs) needs a Coolify token with the read:sensitive ability.

docs.title: CPU fallback
docs.text: The compose file has no CPU fallback worker. The Coolify host has 16 GB RAM and 6 cores, shared with other applications (measured 2026-11-01: 7.7 GB available, 8 GB of swap in use). A faster-whisper large-v3 CPU worker would compete with those applications. Add one only after you measure it on this host and an operator approves it explicitly: enroll it as a separate worker, approve only the cpu-private candidates, and enable cpu_fallback_enabled in the organization settings.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text: Deploy Resona as a set of Docker containers. This is the recommended approach for production and any shared server environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Engine 24+ with the Compose plugin
  • NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed and configured
  • An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.8+ support

GPU requirement

Every engine container (engine-faster-whisper, engine-whisper, engine-voxtral) requires an NVIDIA GPU. The API container is CPU-only and needs no GPU. Without the NVIDIA Container Toolkit the engine containers will fail to start.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository

git clone https://github.com/ecsplico/resona.git
cd resona

2. Create the environment file

cp .env.example .env

Open .env and configure the variables you need. At minimum, set DATA_PATH to a persistent location on your host. See the key variables table below.

3. Start the stack

The compose file uses profiles to control which engine containers start. Activate the profile for the engine you want:

# faster-whisper (recommended default)
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile faster-whisper up -d

# OpenAI Whisper (PyTorch)
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile whisper up -d

# Voxtral / HuggingFace Transformers
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile voxtral up -d

The API container always starts regardless of which profile is active.

4. Verify health

The engine container takes a few minutes on first start while the model downloads. Wait for the health check to pass before the API starts accepting jobs.

# Engine health (port depends on which engine is running)
curl http://localhost:7001/health   # faster-whisper
curl http://localhost:7002/health   # whisper (if started)
curl http://localhost:7003/health   # voxtral (if started)

# API health
curl http://localhost:7000/health

A healthy response looks like:

{"status": "ok", "engine": "faster-whisper", "models": ["large-v3"]}

docs.title: Key variables
docs.text:
The following variables are the most important to set in .env. For the full list see Environment Variables.

Variable Default Description DATA_PATH ./data Host path for persistent data (transcripts, DB, audio files). Mount this as a volume. RESONA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES 209715200 (200 MiB) Upload and worker-result size limit; larger requests get 413. Hub access always needs an org-bound token from resona-admin (run inside the container, e.g. docker compose exec api resona-admin credential issue --organization <id> --role client). RESONA_ENGINE_KEY (unset) Engine auth key for engine-to-engine calls. Auth is disabled when not set. DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL large-v3 faster-whisper model to load DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL large-v3 OpenAI Whisper model to load DEFAULT_VOXTRAL_MODEL openai/whisper-large-v3 HuggingFace model ID for voxtral DEEPGRAM_API_KEY (unset) Activates Deepgram STT + TTS in the engine catalogue ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (unset) Activates ElevenLabs STT + TTS in the engine catalogue OPENAI_API_KEY (unset) Activates OpenAI STT + TTS in the engine catalogue

Persist your data

The compose file mounts ./data inside the API container. Set DATA_PATH=/srv/resona/data (or any path outside the repo) in .env and update the volumes entry in docker-compose.resona.yml accordingly, so transcripts and the SQLite database survive container recreation.

docs.title: GPU setup
docs.text:
Engine containers are built on nvidia/cuda:12.8.0-runtime-ubuntu24.04. Compose requests a GPU via:

deploy:
  resources:
    reservations:
      devices:
        - capabilities: [gpu]

To verify the NVIDIA runtime is available before starting:

docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.8.0-runtime-ubuntu24.04 nvidia-smi

If this fails, check that nvidia-container-toolkit is installed and that the Docker daemon has "default-runtime": "nvidia" set in /etc/docker/daemon.json.

docs.title: Multi-engine deployment
docs.text:
Run multiple engine containers simultaneously and point the API at all of them. The API load-balances across the listed URLs and tracks which engine handled each job.

1. Start multiple engine profiles

docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml \
  --profile faster-whisper \
  --profile whisper \
  up -d

This starts engine-faster-whisper on port 7001 and engine-whisper on port 7002.

2. Configure RESONA_ENGINE_URLS

Add to .env:

RESONA_ENGINE_URLS=http://engine-faster-whisper:7001,http://engine-whisper:7001

The compose file already sets this variable to include all three engine service names. When a profile is inactive its container simply does not start, but the URL remains in the list — the API skips unreachable engines gracefully.

3. Pin a default engine (optional)

RESONA_DEFAULT_ENGINE=faster-whisper

When set, the API routes jobs that do not specify an engine to this one. Without it the API picks the first reachable engine.

docs.title: Logs and restart policy
docs.text:
All containers use restart: unless-stopped. View logs with:

docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml logs -f api
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml logs -f engine-faster-whisper

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile faster-whisper pull
docker compose -f docker-compose.resona.yml --profile faster-whisper up -d

Model weights are cached in ${HOME}/.cache/huggingface on the host (mounted as a volume), so re-pulls do not re-download the model.

docs.title: Full-Stack Setup (uv)
docs.text: Run the engine and API directly on the host with uv. This is the recommended approach for development, staging, and single-machine deployments where Docker is not available.

docs.title: When to use this approach
docs.text:
• Local development — fast iteration without rebuilding images
  • Staging or CI environments — no Docker daemon required
  • Single-machine deployments — engine and API share the same GPU and filesystem

For production multi-machine deployments, see Docker Deployment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• uv installed
  • NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.8+ (engine only; the API is CPU-only)
  • All workspace packages installed:
uv sync --all-packages

docs.title: Start the stack
docs.text:
Open two terminals in the repo root.

Terminal 1 — engine (requires GPU)

uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper   # listens on :7001

Wait until you see a log line like Application startup complete. before starting the API.

Terminal 2 — API

uv run resona-api                      # listens on :7000

Verify

curl http://localhost:7001/health
curl http://localhost:7000/health

A healthy engine response:

{"status": "ok", "engine": "faster-whisper", "models": ["large-v3"]}

docs.title: Switching engines
docs.text:
Use RESONA_ENGINE to select which ASR backend the engine-server loads. Each engine has its own entry-point script.

# OpenAI Whisper (PyTorch)
RESONA_ENGINE=whisper uv run resona-engine-whisper

# Voxtral / HuggingFace Transformers
RESONA_ENGINE=voxtral uv run resona-engine-voxtral

Override the model with the corresponding env var:

DEFAULT_FASTWHISPER_MODEL=medium uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper
DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL=base uv run RESONA_ENGINE=whisper resona-engine-whisper
DEFAULT_VOXTRAL_MODEL=openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo uv run resona-engine-voxtral

docs.title: Multi-engine setup
docs.text:
Start multiple engine instances on different ports and point the API at all of them.

Start engines on separate ports

# Terminal 1
PORT=7001 uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper

# Terminal 2
PORT=7002 RESONA_ENGINE=whisper uv run resona-engine-whisper

Start the API with all engine URLs

# Terminal 3
RESONA_ENGINE_URLS=http://localhost:7001,http://localhost:7002 uv run resona-api

The API probes all listed URLs at startup, tracks which engines are reachable, and load-balances incoming jobs across them. Use RESONA_DEFAULT_ENGINE to pin a default for requests that do not specify an engine.

RESONA_ENGINE_URLS=http://localhost:7001,http://localhost:7002 \
  RESONA_DEFAULT_ENGINE=faster-whisper \
  uv run resona-api

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The hub always requires org-bound credentials. Create an organization and a client token on the hub host; the token is printed once:

uv run resona-admin organization create acme
uv run resona-admin credential issue --organization acme --role client

# Client side
export RESONA_API_URL=http://localhost:7000
export RESONA_API_KEY=<token>

Queued jobs run on pull workers, not on the hub. Prepare the worker on its machine (this verifies cached weights and runs synthetic jobs), then enroll and approve it with the tuples it tested:

uv run resona-worker prepare --profile mac-private --out caps.json      # on the worker machine
uv run resona-worker capabilities caps.json > caps-approve.json

uv run resona-admin worker enroll mac-studio --organization acme   # prints the worker token
uv run resona-admin worker approve <worker-id> --private --capabilities-file caps-approve.json

uv run resona-worker run --hub http://localhost:7000 --token-file ~/.resona/worker.token \
  --capabilities-file caps.json --work-dir /tmp/resona-worker

The token file must have mode 0600. On a Mac, run the worker as a launchd service instead: see Mac Worker. The optional engine key still protects a directly exposed engine-server:

RESONA_ENGINE_KEY=secret-engine-key uv run resona-engine-faster-whisper

Using a .env file

Instead of exporting variables in every terminal, create a .env file in the repo root. python-decouple reads it automatically. Environment variables always take priority over .env values.

docs.title: Cloud providers
docs.text:
Cloud STT and TTS providers activate automatically when their API key is present. No extra configuration is needed — set the key and the provider appears in the engine catalogue.

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... \
  DEEPGRAM_API_KEY=dg-... \
  uv run resona-api

Check the catalogue:

curl http://localhost:7000/v1/engines

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The engine process requires a GPU for model inference. The API process does not use a GPU.
  • Model weights are cached in ${HOME}/.cache/huggingface (HuggingFace models) or the faster-whisper cache directory. First startup downloads the model and is slow; subsequent starts are fast.
  • The API stores jobs and transcripts in DATA_PATH (default ./data). Set this to an absolute path in production to avoid confusion with the working directory.

docs.title: Linux Worker (NVIDIA, Docker)
docs.text:
A resona-worker container on a Linux host with an NVIDIA GPU serves the linux-cuda execution profile:

Kind Engine Model Accelerator audio whisper (openai-whisper, PyTorch) large-v3 CUDA document docling + rapidocr docling-standard CUDA (layout and table structure), CPU (RapidOCR, onnxruntime)

The worker is outbound-only. It long-polls the hub and opens no port. It gets no Docker socket. The hub and the approved worker can read job content. External AI providers cannot: private jobs run with offline model caches, with telemetry disabled and without cloud credentials (see Mac Worker; the same execution subprocess runs in the container).

The host is allowed to be offline. Jobs that the private-auto profile can also run on the Mac stay queued and are claimed by the Mac worker.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• NVIDIA driver and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit (docker info lists the nvidia runtime).
  • The image ships PyTorch built for CUDA 13.0 (torch 2.12.0+cu130, arch list up to sm_120). Blackwell GPUs (RTX 50xx, compute capability 12.0) are supported. The driver must support CUDA 13.0.
  • About 16 GB of disk for the image and 5 GB for the model cache. Whisper large-v3 uses about 9 GB of VRAM.

Check the GPU from inside the image before you prepare:

docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint python <image> -c \
  "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), torch.cuda.get_arch_list())"

docs.title: 1. Build the image
docs.text:
docker build -f apps/resona-worker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=nvidia/cuda:13.0.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04 \
  --build-arg "WORKER_EXTRAS=--extra cuda --extra documents" \
  --build-arg RESONA_RELEASE_ID=<release> \
  -t resona-worker:<release>-cuda .
docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' resona-worker:<release>-cuda    # sha256:… digest

Use the image by digest only (resona-worker@sha256:… locally, or the released ghcr.io/…@sha256:…). Never use :latest or :cuda.

docs.title: 2. Enroll on the hub
docs.text:
On the hub host:

resona-admin worker enroll gpu-pc --organization acme   # prints worker_id and token once

On the Linux host, store the token in a file that only UID 1000 can read. The container user resona has UID 1000 and refuses token files with a wider mode:

mkdir -p ~/resona-worker && cd ~/resona-worker
(umask 077; printf '%s\n' '<token>' > worker.token)

docs.title: 3. Configure docker-compose.worker.yml
docs.text:
Copy docker-compose.worker.yml from the repository root and create .env next to it:

RESONA_WORKER_IMAGE=resona-worker@sha256:<digest>
RESONA_HUB_URL=https://resona.ecsplico.de
RESONA_WORKER_TOKEN_FILE=/home/<user>/resona-worker/worker.token

The service:

Item Setting GPU deploy.resources.reservations.devices: driver nvidia, count: 1, capabilities: [gpu] Model cache named volume models at /models (HF_HOME and the openai-whisper checkpoints under /models/cache) Capabilities manifest named volume state at /state Job directory tmpfs at /work (4 GB, mode 0700): empty after every start, never on disk Token bind mount of the 0600 file at /run/secrets/resona-worker-token, read-only Isolation no ports, no Docker socket, cap_drop: [ALL], no-new-privileges, user UID 1000 Restart unless-stopped

docs.title: 4. Prepare
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml run --rm worker \
  prepare --profile linux-cuda --out /state/capabilities.json

prepare takes the model pins of the image's release (resona_worker/models.json in the resona-worker wheel; --release-manifest selects another manifest) and downloads each missing pinned revision into the models volume: the openai-whisper large-v3 checkpoint (its revision is the published SHA-256, verified after download) and the Docling layout (docling-project/docling-layout-heron) and table-structure (docling-project/docling-models) snapshots at their pinned commits. A model without a pin fails prepare; an unpinned main snapshot is never used. RapidOCR's ONNX models are part of the rapidocr wheel. Add --offline to forbid downloads: a missing pin then fails with its repo@revision. Jobs never download.

Then prepare runs a real synthetic job for each candidate in the private, offline execution subprocess, checks the recognized German words, checks that the primary stage ran on CUDA and that every HuggingFace model the run recorded is the pinned revision. It records seconds, peak RSS, peak CUDA memory (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated) and the device of every stage. If a step fails, prepare exits non-zero and does not change the existing manifest.

Output on an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB, driver 615.78.08):

ok audio: whisper large-v3 [cuda] 20.8s, peak RSS 6823 MiB, peak cuda 8962 MiB; asr:whisper=cuda; large-v3@e5b1a55b89c1
ok document: docling docling-standard [cuda] 18.9s, peak RSS 3197 MiB, peak cuda 575 MiB; layout:docling-layout=cuda, layout:docling-tableformer=cuda, ocr:rapidocr=cpu; docling-project/docling-layout-heron@8f39ad3c0b4c, docling-project/docling-models@fc0f2d45e221
prepared 2 capability tuple(s) for linux-cuda -> /state/capabilities.json

The first run, which downloaded the weights, took about 6 minutes; later runs with the weights cached take about 45 seconds.

docs.title: 5. Approve and run
docs.text:
Print the tested tuples and give them to the hub admin:

docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml run --rm -T worker capabilities /state/capabilities.json > caps-approve.json
resona-admin worker approve <worker-id> --private --capabilities-file caps-approve.json   # on the hub

Start the worker:

docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml logs -f     # never contains content, filenames or tokens
docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml down        # stop; keeps the models and state volumes

Each job runs in its own subprocess. The model is loaded for that job and is released when the subprocess exits, so the GPU is free between jobs.

docs.title: LLM polish on the worker host
docs.text: Document jobs can get an OCR-correction pass from a local model on the worker host. The bundled document-polish-de profile (in the resona-postprocess wheel, resona_postprocess/profiles/document-polish-de.json) sends the Docling Markdown in chunks of about 12000 characters, split on block boundaries and never inside a table, to the endpoint local-llm. The profile names no host: an org admin registers a local_llm endpoint with the id local-llm, a loopback url and the approved worker's worker_id (see Enable it). Its prompt allows only OCR fixes (hyphenation, umlauts/ß, stray characters, merged/split words) and requires headings, tables, page markers and the <!-- image --> / <!-- formula-not-decoded --> placeholders to stay unchanged. A chunk reply that differs from the chunk by more than 30 % in length, or that changes placeholders, heading levels or table shape, is discarded: the raw chunk is kept and the result gets the warning polish_chunk_rejected:<n>:<length|markup>. A chunk that fails 3 calls fails the job (postprocess_failed, retryable); the polish is never skipped silently. markdown is the polished text. The converter's Markdown before polish, tables included, stays in the result's raw_markdown (set whenever a postprocess step changed the Markdown); raw_text is the converter's plain text, which has no tables. See Postprocessing Pipeline.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: The endpoint is a local_llm endpoint. The execution policy admits it for private jobs only with a loopback url, and the hub hands the job only to the worker the endpoint is assigned to (worker_id). The text therefore goes from the worker process to a model server on the same host and nowhere else. A job whose profile uses a local_llm endpoint with a non-loopback url is refused at submission (policy_denied), and the policy is checked again before every chunk. A non-loopback unload_url is already refused when the settings are saved. Before each LLM stage the worker asks the hub for a fresh policy decision; when the hub is unreachable the stage does not start. Calls to local_llm endpoints carry a fixed placeholder API key, never an OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment, and litellm uses its bundled model price map instead of fetching it.

docs.title: Reaching a model server on the host's loopback
docs.text:
On gpu-box, llama-swap listens on the host's 127.0.0.1:9292 (OpenAI-compatible, /v1). A container on the default bridge network cannot reach the host's loopback, and a bridge address such as 172.17.0.1 is not loopback, so the policy would deny it. docker-compose.worker.llm.yml overrides the worker service with network_mode: host. In the host namespace 127.0.0.1 is the host's loopback, so the endpoint URL http://127.0.0.1:9292/v1 reaches llama-swap and passes the loopback check.

The worker still opens no port (it has no listener) and gets no Docker socket. cap_drop: [ALL], no-new-privileges, UID 1000, the read-only token, the tmpfs job directory and the GPU reservation stay as in the base file. Host networking does give the container the host's network namespace, including every service bound to the host's loopback.

Use both files for every command that starts the worker:

docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml -f docker-compose.worker.llm.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.worker.yml -f docker-compose.worker.llm.yml logs -f

docs.title: GPU sharing with llama-swap
docs.text:
llama-swap keeps a loaded model resident until its ttl expires (1800 s for qwen3.6-27b on gpu-box), using most of the 16 GB of VRAM. A whisper large-v3 job (about 9 GB) started in that window would run out of memory. An endpoint can therefore name an unload_url: after the job's last LLM stage on that endpoint, and also when the job fails after calling it, the worker sends POST <unload_url> (no body, 10-second timeout). The request is best effort and never fails the job. A 2xx answer is logged at info level; any other status (for example 404/405 from a server without that route) is logged as a warning with the endpoint id and the status code, and a transport error as a warning with the endpoint id and the exception type. A warning means the model may still hold the GPU. unload_url must be a loopback http(s) URL and is allowed only on local_llm endpoints; anything else is rejected when the settings are validated.

llama-swap's API (from its docs/kb/guides/model-runtime/ttl-and-unloading.md): POST /api/models/unload/<model_id> unloads one model, POST /api/models/unload unloads all models. Older releases offer GET /unload instead, which the worker's POST does not reach (the worker logs the resulting 404/405 as a warning). The llama-swap installed on gpu-box answered 200 to POST /api/models/unload/<model_id>, POST /api/models/unload and GET /unload. Check with curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9292/api/models/unload/qwen3.6-27b on the host.

docs.title: Enable it
docs.text:
1. Deploy a release that contains this feature to the hub and to every worker first. An older hub rejects unload_url in the settings (422); an older worker fails postprocess jobs whose snapshot contains it (invalid_snapshot).
  2. Start the worker with the override (above).

  3. As org admin, add the endpoint to the organization settings. The bundled profile calls the endpoint id local-llm, so register it under that id (or change the profile's endpoint before uploading it). url and unload_url point to the model server on the worker host's loopback; worker_id is the id that resona-admin worker enroll printed for the Linux worker:

    {
  "id": "local-llm",
  "kind": "local_llm",
  "model": "openai/qwen3.6-27b",
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9292/v1",
  "worker_id": "<linux worker id>",
  "unload_url": "http://127.0.0.1:9292/api/models/unload/qwen3.6-27b"
}

    The openai/ prefix makes litellm speak the OpenAI chat API to url; llama-swap receives the model name qwen3.6-27b.

    resona settings get | jq '.settings | .endpoints = ([.endpoints[] | select(.id != "local-llm")] + [input])' \
  - local-llm.json > settings.json
resona settings set --file settings.json

  4. Upload the bundled profile as an organization profile (org admin):

    python -c "from importlib import resources; print(resources.files('resona_postprocess').joinpath('profiles/document-polish-de.json').read_text())" > document-polish-de.json
resona profiles push document-polish-de document-polish-de.json

    (Or copy the file from packages/postprocess/src/resona_postprocess/profiles/ in the repository.)

  5. Request it per document job:

    resona doc scan.pdf --execution-profile linux-cuda --profile document-polish-de --output-dir out/

    Leave the organization settings polish: false: with polish: true and postprocess_profile: "document-polish-de" every job, audio included, would get the document prompt. A job that names the profile is claimed only by the worker that the endpoint is assigned to.

Measured on 2026-11-02 (evaluation corpus, gpu-box, linux-cuda, qwen3.6-27b via llama-swap; CER = character error rate):

Fixture Plain document-polish-de degraded scan 0.002 0.000 small print scan 0.196 0.191 invisible text layer re-OCRed in auto (bad-text-layer) 0.004 0.000 dense table scan 3 cells missing* 0 cells missing French scan, auto (fr-scan-pdf, 2026-11-04, endpoint local-llm) 0.200 0.200 all other fixtures 0.000 0.000

* Before the °℃ normalization (608e6e7); the plain run now also misses no cell.

  • Polish fixes single misread characters. It cannot restore text that OCR dropped, as on the small print scan; --ocr force fixes that case (see CLI doc).
  • It adds 36–77 s per one-page document, including reloading the model, because the worker unloads it after each job.
  • No chunk was rejected by the length or markup guards.
  • The polished markdown is still a model rewrite: keep raw_markdown (the converter's Markdown before polish) as the reference.

docs.title: When CUDA is not available
docs.text: At start, the worker asks the execution environment whether each accelerator of its manifest works (python -m resona_worker.execute --probe-accelerator cuda). If CUDA does not work (no GPU reservation, driver failure, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""), the worker logs cuda is not available on this host; not offering 2 tuple(s) and heartbeats with no CUDA tuples. It never claims a CUDA job that it cannot run. The hub reports such jobs as queue_reason: no_capable_worker (approved tuples that the worker does not offer do not count). private-auto jobs stay eligible for the Mac worker, which claims them when it is online. A prepare without a GPU fails with unsupported_capability and leaves the previous manifest unchanged.

docs.title: Result provenance
docs.text:
Every stage records its real device and, on CUDA/Metal stages, the peak device memory of the job's process (peak_accelerator_bytes). The Docling layout and table-structure stages run in one engine call and share the value:

asr     whisper              large-v3@e5b1a55b…                              cuda  8962 MiB
layout  docling-layout       docling-project/docling-layout-heron@8f39ad3c…  cuda   575 MiB
layout  docling-tableformer  docling-project/docling-models@fc0f2d45…        cuda   575 MiB
ocr     rapidocr             rapidocr-ppocr@3.9.2                            cpu

docs.title: Silence
docs.text: openai-whisper has no voice-activity filter of its own and turns noise into text such as "Vielen Dank.". The engine applies faster-whisper's bundled Silero VAD when the job's vad_filter option is set (the default): only detected speech is decoded, and audio without speech gives an empty transcript.

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: The linux-cuda/linux-cuda baseline in eval/baselines.json was promoted from a remote evaluation on this worker (resona eval --profile linux-cuda --platform linux-cuda --remote, then resona eval promote <id>). See Evaluation & Baselines.

docs.title: Mac Single-Host Stack (Apple Silicon)
docs.text: Run resona-api and an ASR engine on one Apple Silicon Mac, for local development or a single-user setup. For serving jobs from a Mac to a remote hub, use the Mac Worker instead.

docs.title: Why the engine is not in Docker
docs.text:
MLX/Metal cannot run inside a Linux container, and Docker on macOS has no GPU passthrough, so any engine in Docker is CPU-only. The engine therefore runs natively on the Apple GPU and only the api runs in Docker.

Component Where Port Default mlx-whisper engine (GPU, large-v3) native (scripts/run-native-engine.sh) 7720 on api (resona-api) Docker (docker-compose.mac.yml) 7710 on engine-faster-whisper (CPU fallback) Docker, profile cpu-engine 7720 off

The native engine uses mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx, the engine and model recommended_engine() picks on Apple Silicon.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
From the repository root:

scripts/run-native-engine.sh                      # terminal 1: native MLX engine on :7720
docker compose -f docker-compose.mac.yml up -d    # terminal 2: api on :7710

Or just mac-engine and just mac-up.

  • api: http://localhost:7710 (/health, OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/*)
  • engine: http://localhost:7720/health

The first engine start runs uv sync --all-packages --extra apple and downloads the model into ~/.cache/huggingface. Override the engine or model with RESONA_ENGINE, PORT and DEFAULT_MLX_WHISPER_MODEL.

docs.title: Add the PWA data layer
docs.text:
Directus and the project worker live in apps/resona-pwa. Their compose file targets an api on host port 7710 by default, so it works against this stack unchanged:

cd apps/resona-pwa
cp .env.stack.example .env    # set DIRECTUS_TOKEN and RESONA_API_KEY (an org token from resona-admin)
docker compose -f docker-compose.backend.yml up -d

docs.title: CPU-only fallback
docs.text:
Runs faster-whisper in Docker instead of the native engine. It is slow at large-v3 on CPU; set FASTWHISPER_MODEL=small for usable latency.

docker compose -f docker-compose.mac.yml --profile cpu-engine up -d --build

docs.title: Stop
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.mac.yml --profile cpu-engine down   # add --volumes to wipe data

Stop the native engine with Ctrl-C in its terminal.

docs.title: Mac Worker (Apple Silicon)
docs.text:
A native resona-worker on an Apple Silicon Mac serves the mac-private execution profile:

Kind Engine Model Accelerator audio mlx-whisper mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx Metal (MLX) document docling + ocrmac (Apple Vision) docling-standard Metal (layout), Apple Vision (OCR); Docling's table model runs on CPU

Run it natively. Docker on macOS has no access to Metal, MLX or Apple Vision.

The worker is outbound-only. It long-polls the hub over HTTPS and opens no listening port. The hub and the approved worker can read job content. External AI providers cannot: private jobs run with offline model caches, with telemetry disabled and without cloud credentials.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
From a checkout of the repository:

uv sync --all-packages --extra apple --extra documents

The worker uses the workspace .venv (.venv/bin/resona-worker). It does not download weights while it serves jobs. Put the weights into the HuggingFace cache once, while you are online:

uv run hf download mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx
uv run hf download docling-project/docling-layout-heron
uv run hf download docling-project/docling-models --revision v2.3.0

docs.title: 2. Enroll on the hub
docs.text:
On the hub host:

resona-admin worker enroll mac-studio --organization acme   # prints worker_id and token once

On the Mac, store the token in a file that only your user can read. run and install refuse token files with wider modes or symlinks:

(umask 077; printf '%s\n' '<token>' > ~/.resona/worker.token)

Do not put the worker token into ~/.resona/config.json, into environment variables or into command arguments.

docs.title: 3. Prepare
docs.text:
.venv/bin/resona-worker prepare --profile mac-private --out ~/.resona/worker-caps.json

resona worker prepare --profile mac-private … (the unified resona CLI) runs the same command; every resona-worker <command> below is also available as resona worker <command>.

The model revisions come from the release: by default the pins packaged with the installed resona-worker (resona_worker/models.json), or --release-manifest release-manifest.json. A model or Docling stage weight without a pin fails prepare; an unpinned main snapshot is never accepted. For each candidate of the profile, prepare:

  1. makes every model it loads resolve to its pinned commit in the local HuggingFace cache: the ASR model and Docling's layout (docling-project/docling-layout-heron) and table-structure (docling-project/docling-models) weights. A missing pinned commit is downloaded; the branch or tag the engine loads offline (main, v2.3.0) is pointed at that commit. With --offline, prepare never downloads and fails with the missing repo@revision. This happens for all candidates before the first synthetic run.
  2. runs a real synthetic job through the same execution subprocess and private environment as production jobs: a short German WAV for audio and a scanned German PDF for documents. It checks the recognized German words.
  3. checks that the primary stage ran on the requested accelerator (asr on Metal, Docling layout on Metal) and that every HuggingFace model the run recorded in its provenance is the pinned revision.
  4. records seconds, peak RSS, peak Metal memory and the device of every stage.

Use --settings-file settings.json to prepare the organization's current profiles (the body of GET /v1/settings) instead of the seeded defaults. If a step fails, prepare exits non-zero and does not change the existing manifest.

Example output on an M5 Pro (64 GB):

ok audio: mlx-whisper mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx [metal] 2.5s, peak RSS 3473 MiB, peak metal 3838 MiB; asr:mlx-whisper=metal; mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx@49e6aa286ad6
ok document: docling docling-standard [metal] 7.4s, peak RSS 1129 MiB; layout:docling-layout=metal, layout:docling-tableformer=cpu, ocr:ocrmac=metal; docling-project/docling-layout-heron@8f39ad3c0b4c, docling-project/docling-models@fc0f2d45e221

docs.title: 4. Approve
docs.text:
Print the tested tuples and give them to the hub admin:

.venv/bin/resona-worker capabilities ~/.resona/worker-caps.json > caps-approve.json
resona-admin worker approve <worker-id> --private --capabilities-file caps-approve.json   # on the hub

The worker offers a tuple only if it is in both sets: its own tested manifest and the hub-approved list that it receives in every heartbeat reply. The hub also requires an exact tuple match on every claim. A heartbeat cannot widen the approval.

docs.title: 5. Run as a launchd service
docs.text:
.venv/bin/resona-worker install --profile mac-private \
  --hub https://resona.ecsplico.de \
  --token-file ~/.resona/worker.token \
  --capabilities-file ~/.resona/worker-caps.json

This command:

  • writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/de.ecsplico.resona-worker.plist (--label changes the name) and loads it with launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID. The service starts at login and restarts after a crash.
  • puts only the token file path into the plist. The plist environment contains only PATH, PYTHONUNBUFFERED and the HuggingFace cache location; no credentials.
  • refuses a token file with a mode wider than 0600, a hub URL that is not https:// (plain http:// is allowed only for loopback), and a manifest that was prepared for a different profile.
  • uses ~/Library/Caches/resona-worker/<label> as the per-job scratch directory and writes the log to ~/Library/Logs/resona-worker/<label>.log. The log never contains content, filenames or tokens.

Check and remove:

launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/de.ecsplico.resona-worker | grep -E 'state|pid'
.venv/bin/resona-worker uninstall            # boots out the agent and deletes the plist

To run the worker in the foreground instead of as a service:

.venv/bin/resona-worker run --hub https://resona.ecsplico.de --token-file ~/.resona/worker.token \
  --capabilities-file ~/.resona/worker-caps.json --work-dir /tmp/resona-worker

docs.title: Private execution environment
docs.text:
Each job runs in its own subprocess. For private jobs, the subprocess environment is an allowlist: system and locale variables, model-cache paths and engine tuning variables. Names that look like credentials (*_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, …) are always removed, and so are OPENAI*, DEEPGRAM*, ELEVENLABS*, AWS_*, AZURE_*, GOOGLE_*, ANTHROPIC* and RESONA_API_KEY. The worker always sets:

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1  TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1  HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1
HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1  HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1  DO_NOT_TRACK=1

Docling runs in-process. Its remote services stay at the default (disabled), and it loads its layout and table models from the same offline HuggingFace cache.

docs.title: Out of memory
docs.text:
The worker treats a job as out of memory if the engine subprocess is killed with SIGKILL (for example by jetsam), raises MemoryError, or prints an out-of-memory marker such as MLX's [metal::malloc]. The worker then:

  • fails the attempt as retryable out_of_memory. The hub requeues the job until its attempt limit is reached, and another worker can claim it.
  • stops offering that tuple until the worker restarts. The hub records the withdrawal in the job's error message only and keeps the worker's approved capabilities unchanged, so after a restart (and prepare, if memory settings changed) the worker offers the tuple again without a new approval.

docs.title: Apple Vision returns no text
docs.text:
macOS caches compiled Vision models per process name, under ~/Library/Caches/<name>/com.apple.e5rt.e5bundlecache. The worker, the CLI and resona-worker prepare all run as python3. A damaged python3 cache makes accurate recognition return no text on some pages without an error: the job completes with empty Markdown, while fast recognition and other process names still work. Seen on 2026-11-02 (macOS build 26B123): a scanned page came back empty and prepare still passed, because its synthetic scan was not affected.

Fix: stop the worker, move the cache aside (macOS rebuilds it on the next run), then start the worker and run prepare again:

mv ~/Library/Caches/python3 ~/Library/Caches/python3.broken

Check: resona eval --profile mac-private --output-dir /tmp/eval must report CER 0.0 on the scanned fixtures.

docs.title: Result provenance
docs.text:
Every result records the real device of each stage, for example:

asr     mlx-whisper          mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-mlx@49e6aa28…  metal
layout  docling-layout       docling-project/docling-layout-heron@8f39ad3c…  metal
layout  docling-tableformer  docling-project/docling-models@fc0f2d45…        cpu
ocr     ocrmac               apple-vision                                    metal

docs.title: Releases, evaluations and worker updates
docs.text: A Resona release is an immutable pin set: every wheel by name, version and SHA-256, every image by sha256: digest, every model by exact revision. Release ids are package versions (tag v0.2.0 → release 0.2.0); resona-api and resona-worker must both carry it.

docs.title: Release manifest
docs.text:
release-manifest.json (schema release/manifest.schema.json, model resona_job_core.release.ReleaseManifest):

{"release_id": "0.2.0", "created_at": "...", "worker_protocol": 1,
 "wheels": [{"name": "resona-worker", "version": "0.2.0", "sha256": "<64 hex>"}],
 "images": [{"name": "ghcr.io/ecsplico/resona-hub", "digest": "sha256:<64 hex>"}],
 "models": [{"engine": "faster-whisper", "model": "Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3", "revision": "<commit>"}],
 "constraints": {"name": "worker-constraints.txt", "sha256": "<64 hex>"}}

Image names carry no tag; mutable revisions (latest, cuda, main, …) are rejected. Build one locally with uv run python release/build_manifest.py --release-id X --dist dist/ --image NAME=sha256:... --constraints dist/worker-constraints.txt --out dist/release-manifest.json (model pins come from apps/resona-worker/src/resona_worker/models.json, the same file resona-worker prepare uses by default). worker-constraints.txt is uv export --frozen --package resona-worker --all-extras --no-emit-workspace --no-hashes --no-header --no-annotate: the third-party versions from uv.lock, shipped next to the wheels. Without it a fresh worker environment resolves whatever the index serves that day (observed: a newer huggingface_hub that rejects the cached model snapshots).

docs.title: Release pipeline (.github/workflows/release.yml)
docs.text:
On a v* tag: version check, privacy/lease/release/update tests, tool-inventory.json check → uv build --all-packages → hub CPU, worker CPU and worker CUDA images (plus legacy engine images), pushed by version tag and recorded by digest → resona eval --profile cpu-private on eval/corpus against eval/baselines.json → manifest + draft GitHub release with wheels, manifest, worker-constraints.txt, schema and tool-inventory.json as assets.

Repository variables (all optional): RESONA_IMAGE_NAMESPACE (default ghcr.io/ecsplico, unverified), RESONA_PUBLISH_PYPI=true (PyPI trusted publishing; namespace unverified, so GitHub release assets are canonical), RESONA_DISPATCH_MCP_RELEASE=true with repo secrets RELEASE_DISPATCH_APP_ID/RELEASE_DISPATCH_APP_KEY to dispatch mcp-release ({mcp: "resona-hub", version, tools}, same shape as skaile-ai/excel-mcp) to skaile-ai/ai-assets, whose mcp-release-bump.yml opens the catalog bump PR for mcp/resona-hub/MCP.md and diffs its tool block against tools. Not to skaile-ai/platform: its mcp-release handler only adopts flake-pinned stdio servers. The secrets are the skaile-release-dispatch GitHub App's id and private key; in skaile-ai they are organization secrets, which this ecsplico repository does not inherit, so a skaile-ai org owner must add them here (unset as of 2026-11-01). Regenerate the inventory with uv run python scripts/gen_tool_inventory.py after changing MCP tools.

docs.title: Hub: staging, evaluation, approval
docs.text:
resona-admin release stage --manifest release-manifest.json   # admits the release for evaluation jobs only
resona-admin release list                                     # releases and approved (org, profile, platform) tuples
  • GET /v1/version (no auth) → {release_id, hub_version, worker_protocol}.
  • Evaluation jobs: POST /v1/jobs with purpose: "evaluation" needs an org_admin credential and a release_id the hub knows (staged or bundled), else 403 / 422 release_not_staged.
  • POST /v1/evaluations (org_admin; metrics, corpus hash, gate only — no text) → GET /v1/evaluations/{id} → POST /v1/evaluations/{id}/promote with expected_baseline_revision (409 baseline_revision_mismatch, 422 gate_failed). GET /v1/baselines?execution_profile=&platform= → current baseline or 404 baseline_required.
  • Complete metrics: every recorded evaluation carries fixture_checks ({fixture_id: {kind, checks}}, as the corpus manifest declares them; resona eval --remote sends it) and every fixture must have exactly the metrics its checks produce (wer→wer, cer→cer, silence→silence_insertions, table_cells→missing_cells, reading_order→order_failures), else 422 incomplete_metrics. An empty metrics object can therefore never pass the absolute checks.
  • Gate: the first baseline needs passing absolute checks (no missing cells, order failures or silence insertions); later ones also have every baseline fixture and metric and no WER/CER regression above 0.02.
  • Changed corpus: if the current baseline of the same (execution profile, platform) was measured on another corpus_sha256, promotion answers 409 baseline_corpus_mismatch, unless the admin sends "rebaseline": true (resona eval promote <id> --rebaseline). That promotion starts the new corpus's baseline on absolute checks only; later promotions compare against it.
  • Promotion approves (execution_profile, platform, release_id) for the organization. Production jobs are claimed only by workers whose reported release is approved for that tuple; otherwise the job waits with queue_reason: release_not_approved.
  • Bootstrap: the hub's own release (RESONA_RELEASE_ID, else the installed resona-api version) is the bundled release, recorded by migration 2 and at every startup. It may run evaluation jobs without being staged, but like any release it runs production jobs only for tuples approved by a promoted evaluation. A new deployment therefore runs resona eval --remote and resona eval promote once per (execution profile, platform) before production jobs are claimed. Staging the bundled release's real manifest replaces its placeholder and keeps it bundled.

docs.title: Worker protocol
docs.text: Workers send X-Resona-Worker-Protocol: 1. Every worker route (heartbeat, claim, input, postprocess, policy, result, fail) answers 426 protocol_incompatible for any other major before touching content.

docs.title: Updating a worker
docs.text:
Run on the worker machine (the hub cannot trigger updates):

resona-worker update --version 0.2.0 --manifest https://.../release-manifest.json \
  --profile mac-private --hub https://resona.example --token-file ~/.resona/worker.token \
  --capabilities-file caps.json --work-dir ~/Library/Caches/resona-worker/work [--label <launchd label>]

Order: manifest names --version → hub reports the release staged/approved for this org with the same manifest digest → wheels and worker-constraints.txt downloaded and SHA-256 verified → drain (the running worker finishes its current job, then stops claiming) → install only the resona-worker wheel (profile extras) into <releases-dir>/<id>/venv, with every other pinned wheel as a direct-URL constraint plus the locked third-party constraints → prepare with the manifest's model pins into a new capabilities file. Only if prepare succeeds is the capabilities file replaced, current repointed and the service restarted; on any failure (e.g. a model revision the local cache does not hold) the previous release and capabilities stay, the drain is released and the command exits nonzero.

The drain handshake lives in the work directory: the supervisor records its pid (supervisor.pid), update writes drain, the supervisor answers drained between jobs. If no supervisor is alive the wait ends at once (nothing can be claiming; the drain request stays, so a worker started meanwhile drains before its first claim). Without --label there is no service to restart: after a successful update the old supervisor is told (superseded) to exit instead of resuming on old code, and the command prints the new release's run line. Linux Docker workers update by pulling the manifest's pinned image digest, not with this command.
